easy.def: The words people use to talk and write.
examples: Spanish is a language.
Babies learn language by listening.
Sign language uses your hands.

more.def: A system of words that people use to speak, write, and understand each other.
examples: She can speak three languages: English, French, and Arabic.
People who cannot hear may use sign language.
He is learning a new language before his trip.
I heard laughter from the playground.
The joke filled the room with laughter.
Laughter is a happy sound.

more.def: The sound or act of laughing.
examples: The room filled with laughter when the clown came in.
Their laughter could be heard down the hall.
The funny movie brought tears of laughter.

easy.def: Not wanting to work or move.
examples: The lazy cat slept all day.
I feel lazy on hot days.
A lazy dog lay in the sun.

more.def: Not willing to work or use energy.
examples: He felt too lazy to get up and close the door.
We spent a lazy afternoon reading by the pool.
He was too lazy to put his dishes in the sink.

easy.def: The person in front who shows the way.
examples: Today I am the line leader.
The leader of the band waved a stick.
Follow the leader!

more.def: A person who guides or is in charge of a group.
examples: A good leader listens to everyone on the team.
The team chose her as leader because she is fair.
The scout leader showed us how to build a fire.

easy.def: A very old story that people still tell.
examples: There is a legend about a dragon in this cave.
The legend is about a brave girl.
Grandpa told us a legend.

more.def: An old story passed down over many years that may or may not be true.
examples: According to legend, a giant made these hills.
The legend says a monster lives in the lake.
Many legends are told about the brave king.

easy.def: A place with lots of books you can borrow.
examples: I got a book from the library.
The library is a quiet place.
Our school has a library.

more.def: A place where books and other materials are kept for people to read or borrow.
examples: We go to the library every Saturday to choose new books.
You need a card to borrow books from the library.
The library offers story time for young children.

easy.def: A bright flash of light in the sky in a storm.
examples: I saw lightning and then heard thunder.
Lightning hit the tall tree.
The lightning was so bright.

more.def: A bright flash of electricity in the sky during a storm.
examples: Lightning lit up the whole sky for a second.
Never stand under a tree when there is lightning.
We counted the seconds between the lightning and the thunder.

easy.def: Something wet that you can pour.
examples: Water and milk are liquids.
Juice is a liquid.
The soap is a blue liquid.

more.def: Something that flows and can be poured, like water. It is not a solid or a gas.
examples: When ice melts, it changes from a solid into a liquid.
Honey is a thick liquid that pours slowly.
The nurse measured the liquid medicine in a spoon.

easy.def: To use your ears to hear.
examples: Listen to the birds sing.
I listen to music.
Please listen to the story.

more.def: To pay attention so that you can hear something.
examples: If you listen closely, you can hear the ocean from here.
We listened to the rain on the roof.
A good friend listens when you have a problem.

easy.def: Sad because you are by yourself.
examples: The new kid felt lonely at lunch.
The lonely dog wanted a friend.
I feel lonely when you are away.

more.def: Feeling sad because you are alone or have no one to talk to.
examples: He felt lonely after his best friend moved away.
The lighthouse stood on a lonely stretch of coast.
She was lonely at first, but soon made new friends.
My dog is loyal to me.
A loyal friend is always there for you.
The loyal knight helped the king.

more.def: Always faithful and true to a person, group, or idea.
examples: A loyal friend stands by you even when things are hard.
The team has loyal fans who come to every game.
He stayed loyal to his friends when others teased them.

easy.def: Having good things happen to you.
examples: I was lucky to find a coin.
This is my lucky hat.
You are lucky to have a big yard.

more.def: Having good things happen by chance.
examples: We were lucky that the rain stopped just before the game.
He felt lucky to have such kind grandparents.
It was a lucky guess, but it was right.
